lines.d: Here's our web app in two minutes: what it shows, how the data flows, and the rules your code has to follow.
lines.s: Here's our web app, in two minutes: what it shows, how the data flows, and the rules your code has to follow.

lines.d: Fire satellites take a snapshot at about the same time every day.
lines.s: Fire satellites take a snapshot at about the same time every day.

lines.d: But NASA's Aqua satellite has drifted: its 1:30 PM snapshot now happens near 3:50 PM over the Amazon, and Terra is sliding earlier.
lines.s: But NASA's Aqua satellite has drifted. Its one-thirty P M snapshot now happens near three-fifty P M, over the Amazon, and Terra is sliding earlier.

lines.d: Fire activity changes through the day, so the counts shift even when the fires don't.
lines.s: Fire activity changes through the day, so the counts shift, even when the fires don't.

lines.d: And Brazil's official fire record still uses Aqua as its reference.
lines.s: And Brazil's official fire record still uses Aqua as its reference.

lines.d: So VIIRS, which still looks at a fixed time, becomes our clock.
lines.s: So veers, which still looks at a fixed time, becomes our clock.

lines.d: We learn the Aqua-to-VIIRS ratio for each region and month from 2012 to 2020, before the drift.
lines.s: We learn the Aqua-to-veers ratio for each region and month, from twenty twelve to twenty twenty, before the drift.

lines.d: VIIRS times that ratio is a fixed-clock count, in Aqua units.
lines.s: Veers, times that ratio, is a fixed-clock count, in Aqua units.

lines.d: The gap between the real Aqua count and that number shows how far an Aqua-based record has drifted.
lines.s: The gap between the real Aqua count and that number shows how far an Aqua-based record has drifted.

lines.d: That's the app: a fixed-clock fire calendar for anywhere. Pick one of six preset regions.
lines.s: That's the app: a fixed-clock fire calendar, for anywhere. Pick one of six preset regions.

lines.d: The calendar covers every month since 2002, colored by count or by anomaly against the historical median, with a CSV download.
lines.s: The calendar covers every month since two thousand two, colored by count, or by anomaly against the historical median, with a C S V download.

lines.d: The audit panel shows that gap for every year since 2021, with error bars.
lines.s: The audit panel shows that gap for every year since twenty twenty-one, with error bars.

lines.d: Next, the drift chart, and our centerpiece, the two-clocks test: Terra and Aqua drift in opposite directions, so comparing them isolates the clock effect.
lines.s: Next, the drift chart, and our centerpiece, the two-clocks test. Terra and Aqua drift in opposite directions, so comparing them isolates the clock effect.

lines.d: Then California's detection limits, checked against real recorded fires, and a “How do we know?” checklist.
lines.s: Then California's detection limits, checked against real, recorded fires. And a "how do we know" checklist.

lines.d: Under the hood, a Python pipeline turns NASA FIRMS hotspots into small JSON files, one per panel, per region.
lines.s: Under the hood, a Python pipeline turns NASA firms hotspots into small Jason files, one per panel, per region.

lines.d: The app is static and reads only those files.
lines.s: The app is static, and reads only those files.

lines.d: Until the real ones land in data/out, build against data/mock: same layout, same fields.
lines.s: Until the real ones land in data slash out, build against data slash mock. Same layout, same fields.

lines.d: Five rules.
lines.s: Five rules.

lines.d: Mock data always shows a MOCK badge.
lines.s: Mock data always shows a mock badge.

lines.d: Null means no data, not zero.
lines.s: Null means no data. Not zero.

lines.d: Hatch provisional months and mark outages.
lines.s: Hatch provisional months, and mark outages.

lines.d: Show “not enough fires to measure” instead of a noisy number.
lines.s: Show "not enough fires to measure", instead of a noisy number.

lines.d: And every number on screen comes from the JSON.
lines.s: And every number on screen comes from the Jason.

lines.s: Start with the mock data read-me. Let's build it.
